findings.reason: the case must either carry its own mutation (state that it re-applies a case-(1)-style change before reading) or be reordered ahead of case (4), otherwise the node cannot produce the evidence the plan demands.
findings.text: §13's case (5) reads "After case (1)'s change, `_covered_files_for_project` … scans exactly the moved directory", but case (4) of the same list has already established that case (1)'s read re-persists the moved directory's identity ("A second cold read after case (1)'s change … scans no directory"), so at the point case (5) runs every recorded directory matches and the reader scans none; case (5)'s assertion cannot hold in the sequence the list prescribes, and a worker following it literally reaches either a red case it cannot write or a re-mutation the plan never states

findings.reason: unless the plan states that requirement as part of the deliverable, the control passes on the unfixed-shaped behaviour and case (4) measures nothing, so the persistence the plan leans on is left unguarded.
findings.text: §13's case (4) control ("persist only the scanned directories' identities, and the second read scans again") does not necessarily produce the observable it claims, because it removes persisted state rather than adding it: a `_reuse_covered` that iterates the recorded stamps, finds each one unchanged and returns the persisted entries (metadata_index.py:397-408). A reader is made to reuse less, not to walk more; only an implementation that separately refuses a persisted entry whose parent directory carries no recorded stamp falls back to the walk
